mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of corporate shareholder's certificate of incorporation and statutory representative extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry, notary, or Chamber of Commerce of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Convention of 5 October 1961 issued by the origin state's competent authority; if the origin state is not an Apostille party, French Consular Legalization is required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft SAS articles of association (statuts) signed by all shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All shareholders acting by private signature (sous seing privé) or a French notary (acte authentique) where an in-kind contribution of real estate is made
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private signature or notarial deed; no apostille is required for the statuts filed domestically, but any foreign executing signatory's capacity must be evidenced by an apostilled or consularly legalized power of attorney

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration form and supporting ownership chart with evidentiary identity documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SAS legal representative with the assistance of professional counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Electronic filing with the RNE/INPI through the Guichet Unique; underlying passports and certificates for non-French documents must be apostilled or consularly legalized and translated into French by a certified translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Attestation de dépôt de fonds (blocked share capital deposit certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French credit institution (établissement de crédit) holding the deposited capital in a blocked account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original bank certificate issued in the name of the company in formation; no apostille is required; if the certificate originates from a foreign bank, it must be apostilled, certified, and professionally translated into French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (procuration) for the execution of incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each shareholder and signatory, including foreign corporate representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signature verified before a French notary; for signatures executed abroad, the power of attorney must be apostilled under the Hague Convention or submitted to French Consular Legalization in non-Apostille states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation AML/CFT screening of all shareholders, directors, statutory representatives, and UBOs against (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, (iii) the French Treasury asset-freeze table (Liste des gels d'avoirs de la DG Trésor), and (iv) OFAC SDN and UK HMT sanctions lists where USD or GBP payment rails are used. Politically Exposed Person (PEP) identification is required under CMF Article L.561-10-2 and Directive (EU) 2015/849 Article 3(9), with enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification for any PEP or any UBO resident in a FATF high-risk jurisdiction. The SAS must designate a compliance officer responsible for ongoing monitoring and for filing suspicious activity declarations to TRACFIN under CMF Article L.561-15.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.screening_responsible_authorities_note: TRACFIN (French Financial Intelligence Unit), ACPR (Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority), and DG Trésor are the competent supervisory and intelligence authorities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) operated by INPI — formalities submitted through the Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Toubon Law (Loi n° 94-665 du 4 août 1994) and Code de commerce Article L.123-1-7, all mandatory filings and statutory documents submitted to the RNE must be drafted in French. The corporate denomination may contain foreign, invented, or cross-border terms, but any non-Latin script must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet and the official registered name must be set out in French-language form on the Kbis registration certificate.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: French law does not provide for a separate company-name reservation procedure; the denomination is cleared and frozen only when the full incorporation file is submitted through the Guichet Unique and accepted for registration at the RNE. If the RNE registrar rejects the denomination as identical or confusingly similar to a prior registration or protected trademark, the applicant must refile a corrected dossier through the same portal. No statutory extension of a reservation is available because no reservation is granted. The rejection of the incorporation filing can be challenged before the competent tribunal judiciaire (commercial chamber) under the general civil procedure rules and Code de commerce Articles R.123-4 et seq.; a third party claiming prior trademark rights may bring injunctive relief under Code de la propriété intellectuelle Articles L.713-2 et seq. and L.716-4-6, and an unfair competition action (concurrence déloyale) may be initiated before the commercial court. A formal appeal against an administrative refusal by INPI can be filed with the administrative court (tribunal administratif) within two months of notification.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.functioning_note: The 0-day entry above reflects that no legally binding pre-reservation is issued under French registry practice; only the contemporaneous RNE filing secures the name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Generally permitted for a French SAS under Code de commerce Article L.123-11-1 through approved commercial domiciliation providers (sociétés de domiciliation commerciale). For the proposed commercial litigation and arbitration scope, a virtual office is acceptable as the administrative registered seat of the SAS. However, where the SAS operates reserved legal services through admitted avocats, the French national internal rules of the legal profession (Règlement Intérieur National de la profession d'avocat) require a physical professional establishment within the territorial jurisdiction of the relevant bar, making a purely virtual office impermissible for the conduct of such regulated practice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to Moderate: approximately 10% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection during the first 24 months for a low-risk standard-tier SAS in arbitration and asset-tracing services. The probability rises to approximately 35% where the entity operates regulated contentious legal practice, receives funds in a trust/IOLTA-type account, or is domiciled at a third-party virtual address without independent substance. All inspection findings are reviewed against the requirement of a real seat (siège réel) under Article 1835 of the Code civil.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce, Articles L. 227-1 et seq. (Sociétés par actions simplifiées)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte de création de la société
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement for SAS; capital freely determined by shareholders. No escrow account required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company shall be incorporated as a French Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) pursuant to the Code de commerce, with an initial share capital of one hundred thousand euros (EUR 100,000), divided into one hundred thousand shares of one euro par value each. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be located at [full address], France. RESOLVED, that [Full Name], residing at [address], be appointed as the sole gérant (managing director) of the Company, with all powers of administration and legal representation as provided by law. RESOLVED, that the initial share capital be subscribed as follows: [Subscriber Name] subscribes to one hundred thousand (100,000) shares for a total amount of EUR 100,000. This resolution is passed unanimously by the founding shareholders and empowers the gérant to file the Acte de création with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, pay the associated fees, and publish the necessary notices in the BODACC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Corporate Statutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts de la société in French, including company name, registered office, share capital, object of the company, and manager appointments. Sign the statuts and acte de création by all founders. Submit the package to the greffe via the official online portal or in person, accompanied by proof of payment of the filing fee.
required_dossiers: Acte de création de la société
Copies of identity documents of founders and gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the applicant may provide additional documents or amend the statutes within a 15-day period to cure any deficiencies.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), including the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and, for non-established foreign businesses, the Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères (SIEE). The principal digital portal is impots.gouv.fr, with business tax administration conducted through the espace professionnel.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS obtains its SIREN and SIRET identifiers through registration with the competent business formalities authority via the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI). Following registration, the entity is assigned a French tax account by the DGFiP and applies for a VAT identification number through the competent SIE, generally using the registration and tax-account information supplied in the incorporation and tax-registration filings. The VAT number is validated through the VIES system for intra-Community transactions. A foreign entity without a French establishment applies to the SIEE or other competent DGFiP service using the applicable foreign-business registration process, supplies constitutional documents, proof of business activity, identification of representatives, bank and customer information where requested, and appoints a French fiscal representative only where required under the applicable EU or non-EU rules. Registration is required before conducting transactions for which French VAT is due or before making intra-Community acquisitions or supplies requiring identification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). A qualifying SAS incorporated for fewer than five years may elect temporarily for income-tax treatment under the French pass-through regime, subject to statutory conditions concerning size, ownership, activity, and shareholder composition; the election is limited in duration and must be exercised with the DGFiP within the prescribed period. A qualifying family-owned SAS may also elect for the family-company partnership regime where the statutory requirements are met. France does not provide a general United States-style check-the-box election. French anti-hybrid mismatch rules implement the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directives and can deny deductions, impose inclusion, or otherwise neutralize arrangements involving hybrid instruments, entities, or imported mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French value added tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or TVA), harmonized within the European Union VAT system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French-established business, VAT registration is generally required when it carries out taxable transactions outside the applicable franchise en base de TVA. For services, the principal franchise thresholds are EUR 37,500 for prior-year turnover and EUR 41,250 for current-year turnover; for goods, accommodation, and food sales, the principal thresholds are EUR 85,000 and EUR 93,500 respectively. Threshold rules and amounts are subject to legislative change. Voluntary registration is permitted, and registration may be required irrespective of turnover for intra-Community transactions, imports, exports, reverse-charge transactions, or transactions for which the business elects to charge VAT. A French SAS providing professional legal services should obtain a VAT number where its transaction profile requires it, even if a small-business exemption might otherwise be available.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not currently operate a universal real-time invoice-clearance system for ordinary domestic business-to-business transactions. Mandatory electronic invoicing is being phased in under the French Finance Act framework: all French-established businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; issuance obligations apply from 1 September 2026 to large and mid-sized businesses and from 1 September 2027 to small and micro-enterprises not otherwise covered earlier. Invoices must pass through an approved private platform or the public invoicing platform designated by the applicable framework, with structured data transmission and e-reporting for specified cross-border and business-to-consumer transactions. Public-sector invoices are submitted through Chorus Pro. VAT invoices must contain the statutory particulars, including supplier and customer identity, VAT numbers where required, invoice date and number, taxable amount, VAT rate or exemption basis, and reverse-charge wording where applicable. There is no general digital tax stamp requirement for ordinary invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from France to destinations outside the European Union may be exempt from French VAT where the supplier, or an authorized intermediary acting for the supplier, can substantiate that the goods physically left the EU customs territory and satisfy the statutory export conditions. The supplier must retain customs evidence and link the export movement to the invoice and accounting records. Intra-Community supplies of goods may be exempt where the customer is VAT-identified in another EU Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, and the supplier holds the required VAT number and transport evidence. For cross-border legal and litigation services, the result is generally determined by the place-of-supply rules rather than by a conventional export zero rate: B2B services supplied to a customer established outside France are generally located where the customer is established and are invoiced without French VAT, subject to evidence of customer status and applicable reverse-charge rules. B2C services, services connected with French proceedings or immovable property, and other special-category services may remain subject to French VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration and export accompanying or exit confirmation, including the Movement Reference Number where applicable
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, delivery terms, and VAT exemption basis
Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note, courier proof of delivery, or equivalent carrier documentation
Packing list and, where relevant, import clearance or destination-country customs evidence
Proof linking the goods, invoice, customs declaration, and accounting records
For intra-Community supplies: customer VAT identification number validated through VIES and transport evidence to the other EU Member State

For exported legal services: engagement letter, customer tax or business identification, evidence of customer establishment outside France, service records, invoice, and reverse-charge or non-French-place-of-supply notation where applicable

Bank records or other payment evidence where relevant to establish the transaction, noting that French law does not generally require an inward-remittance certificate as a condition for export VAT exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.mandatory_fx_repatriation_deadline_days: Not applicable. France does not impose a general statutory 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline as a condition for claiming export VAT exemption or refund. Export proceeds remain subject to ordinary accounting, banking, anti-money-laundering, sanctions, and transfer-pricing controls.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGFiP may deny the VAT exemption or refund and reassess VAT where the supplier cannot prove export, intra-Community transport, customer VAT status, or the applicable place of supply. Reassessed VAT may include late-payment interest and tax penalties, commonly 5% for certain late-payment situations, 10% for late filing or payment, 40% for deliberate failure or serious non-compliance, and up to 80% for fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of rights, subject to the facts and statutory procedures. Incorrect invoices may trigger VAT liability, correction obligations, and refusal of the customer's deduction. Fraudulent customs declarations may result in customs duties and taxes, customs fines, seizure or confiscation, and criminal prosecution. False documentation, fictitious exports, or knowingly abusive VAT refund claims may also create personal criminal exposure for responsible officers and may lead to recovery of improperly refunded amounts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France operates under a fully convertible Eurozone regime. Capital account transactions are highly convertible with minimal regulatory approvals. Current account transactions, including profit remittances and dividends, face no convertibility barriers beyond standard tax compliance, beneficial ownership verification, and SIREN/SIRET reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion requirements for export proceeds under EU directives. Exporters must file customs declarations and tax returns within 30 days of receipt. Free convertibility applies; ratios are market-driven with no statutory mandates.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Offshore digital EMIs are viable for cross-border operations but require ACPR authorization and compliance with e-money directives; legal constraints include strict AML monitoring, reserve requirements, and cross-border transfer reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding is permitted for standard corporate clients via video KYC and electronic signatures; physical presence mandated only for entities with complex ownership structures or high-risk profiles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive source of wealth documentation, independent legal opinions, and enhanced due diligence reports
Ultimate beneficial owner declarations, corporate structure charts, and notarized certificates

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections routed via SWIFT MT103 using IBAN references and purpose codes such as 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION' or 'SHARE CAPITAL'. Verification requires SIREN/SIRET numbers, beneficial ownership proofs, and tax compliance certifications.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements cleared through SWIFT MT103 for direct wires and Commercial Letters of Credit (LCs) governed by UCP 600. Correspondent banking networks in EUR and USD facilitate settlements with full audit trails.

mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax rate; an additional 3.3% social contribution on corporate income tax may apply to companies meeting the statutory turnover threshold, producing an effective rate of approximately 25.83% on the relevant tax amount.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible small and medium-sized companies may apply a 15% reduced corporate income tax rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, subject to statutory conditions, including turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, fully paid-up share capital, and at least 75% direct or indirect ownership by individuals or qualifying entities. France also provides specific incentives for qualifying intellectual property income, innovation expenditure, and certain investment activities; eligibility is fact-specific and requires statutory documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD, Corporate Income Tax Return, filed electronically through the French tax administration business portal at impots.gouv.fr using EFI, or through an authorized EDI-TDFC provider. Principal financial annexes generally include Forms 2050-SD through 2059-SD. A French SAS must also file the applicable annual transfer-pricing declaration on Form 2257-SD where the statutory conditions are met.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; corporate income tax instalments are generally paid quarterly, with a final balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is generally due within three months after the end of the financial year. For a financial year ending on 31 December, the return is generally due on the second business day following 1 May of the following year. The final corporate income tax balance is generally due by the fifteenth day of the fourth month following year-end, subject to the specific statutory calendar and electronic filing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SAS legal name, registered office, SIREN number, tax identification information, financial year opening and closing dates, tax office, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder is not entered as the taxpayer unless it operates the French business through a taxable French permanent establishment. The French SAS remains the corporate income tax filer and must report its French legal and tax identifiers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the applicable corporate income tax regime, tax consolidation status, parent-company regime where relevant, and special exemption or incentive regimes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State whether the SAS is owned by a foreign parent and disclose French tax consolidation or parent-subsidiary regime positions. Foreign ownership does not remove French corporate income tax filing obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit or loss to taxable profit or loss by reporting permanent additions, permanent deductions, temporary timing differences, non-deductible expenses, exempt income, and tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude foreign-source items not attributable to the French SAS or its French permanent establishment, but include related-party charges and cross-border expenses where they are economically connected to the French activity and adequately documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax losses carried forward or carried back and losses utilized in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign parent-company losses cannot be offset against French SAS profits. French tax losses are subject to French utilization limits and must be supported by accounting continuity and business-activity documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report tax credits, withholding tax credits, foreign tax credits where permitted, and other statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign taxes may be creditable only under an applicable treaty or French domestic rule and only to the extent of the relevant French tax. Maintain foreign tax certificates and evidence of beneficial entitlement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report taxable income, applicable rate, corporate income tax liability, instalments, credits, and final amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not apply treaty relief directly to the SAS's corporate income tax unless a specific treaty allocation rule applies. Treaty relief principally affects shareholder-level withholding, permanent-establishment attribution, and foreign tax credit treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report qualifying disposals, securities transactions, capital gains, capital losses, and applicable participation exemption or long-term capital-gain adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder's disposal of SAS shares is generally analyzed separately under the applicable tax treaty and French domestic rules. The SAS must report its own asset disposals and cannot treat shareholder-level gains as corporate items.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose the nature and aggregate amount of transactions with associated enterprises, including goods, services, financing, royalties, guarantees, and restructurings, where the statutory filing threshold applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border transactions with the foreign parent, group entities, foreign branches, and other associated enterprises. Amounts must reconcile with the general ledger, statutory accounts, VAT records, and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 2067-SD, deductible interest and related-party expense disclosures
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose specified interest, commissions, royalties, and other payments to related parties where the statutory reporting requirements apply.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include payments to foreign group companies and substantiate deductibility, arm's-length pricing, business purpose, withholding-tax treatment, and beneficial ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report qualifying foreign financial accounts or digital-asset accounts held, used, or controlled by the French entity where required by French law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign bank account used for operating receipts, client funds, or litigation-related payments must be separately assessed for disclosure, anti-money-laundering, accounting, and professional-client-money compliance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed corporate income tax returns generally attract a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% where the taxpayer fails to regularize after formal notice and potentially 80% in cases involving fraudulent maneuvers or abusive conduct. Late-payment interest is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Incorrect returns may generate tax reassessment, interest, penalties, and criminal exposure for fraud. Electronic filing failures may also trigger administrative sanctions where paper filing was not permitted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2571-SD for corporate income tax instalments and Form 2572-SD for the corporate income tax balance, filed electronically through impots.gouv.fr or an authorized EDI-TDFC channel.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly instalments and one annual final balance payment.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Corporate income tax instalments are generally due on the fifteenth day of the relevant months in February, May, August, and November. The final balance is generally due by the fifteenth day of the fourth month following the financial year-end, with special timing for 31 December year-ends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the required instalment based on the prior year's corporate income tax or the current year's estimated liability where permitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign shareholder does not pay the SAS's instalments. The French SAS must calculate instalments using its own French taxable base and cannot net the amount against foreign parent-company tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter final corporate income tax due, instalments already paid, tax credits, and the residual balance or overpayment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the balance to Form 2065-SD, the general ledger, bank payment evidence, and any approved tax credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or insufficient instalments generally produce late-payment interest and a 5% surcharge for late payment of tax, subject to the applicable procedural rules. An incorrect estimate does not automatically create a penalty if the underpayment is not intentional and the final liability is properly declared, but repeated or deliberate underpayment may result in reassessment and aggravated penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% French withholding tax is generally imposed on dividends and other distributed income paid by a French company to a non-resident shareholder, subject to domestic exemptions and treaty relief. A qualifying EU parent may obtain a 0% exemption under the French implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally requiring the minimum participation, holding-period, legal-form, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the shareholder should provide a valid certificate of tax residence and the applicable French treaty-relief form, generally Form 5000-FR together with Form 5001-FR for dividends, or the relevant Form 5002-FR or 5003-FR for interest and royalties. The payer must verify residence, beneficial ownership, treaty entitlement, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test issues, minimum holding conditions, and anti-abuse requirements. Relief may be granted at source where the procedural conditions are satisfied; otherwise, French withholding is paid and a refund claim is filed with the competent French tax authority using the appropriate forms and supporting evidence. The French SAS must retain board resolutions, shareholder registers, payment records, residence certificates, treaty forms, and evidence supporting the recipient's beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French-source royalties and similar payments to non-residents are generally subject to 25% withholding tax under domestic law, subject to treaty reduction or exemption and, where applicable, the EU Interest and Royalties Directive. Interest paid by a French SAS to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax under domestic law, although specific statutory rules, anti-abuse provisions, payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions, and treaty provisions may alter the result. Treaty rates vary by recipient state and payment type; a treaty residence certificate and beneficial-owner analysis are required. Deductibility of interest is separately limited by French thin-capitalization, earnings-stripping, anti-hybrid, and general arm's-length rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million threshold for the principal French master-file and local-file documentation obligation, generally based on the French entity's turnover or gross assets, or on specified group and controlled-entity circumstances under French law. A separate annual simplified transfer-pricing declaration generally applies to taxpayers meeting the lower EUR 50 million threshold or other statutory group conditions. The precise filing obligation must be tested against the entity's ownership, group, and transaction profile.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no single standalone economic substance regulation equivalent to a dedicated offshore ESR statute. Substance is enforced through transfer-pricing rules, the beneficial-ownership requirement, the general anti-abuse rule, the principal-purpose test in treaties, controlled foreign company rules, anti-hybrid rules, permanent-establishment principles, abuse-of-law doctrine, and business-purpose requirements. The SAS should maintain French decision-making capacity, appropriate personnel or outsourced operational capability, premises or operational infrastructure proportionate to its activities, contemporaneous records, client and matter files, bank-account control, genuine litigation services, and commercially supportable intercompany arrangements. A conduit, circular cash flow, nominal director structure, or unsupported royalty, management-fee, financing, or legal-services charge may be recharacterized or denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and fraudulent accounting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing litigation revenue, omitting taxable fees, maintaining parallel books, fabricating expenses, routing client or success fees through undisclosed accounts, or intentionally understating taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, 40% or 80% tax penalties depending on conduct, and potential criminal tax-fraud sanctions including imprisonment and substantial fines. Criminal consequences depend on the facts, intent, amount, and prosecution decision.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face personal criminal liability, civil tax liability for fraudulent or seriously negligent conduct, asset recovery, director disqualification, and possible restrictions on leaving France during criminal proceedings. Imprisonment is possible for aggravated tax fraud; a corporate veil is not a protection against personal participation in the offense.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging unsupported foreign management fees, royalties, financing costs, or legal-support fees; allocating French-created profits to a low-tax affiliate; failing to document intercompany transactions; or using non-arm's-length cost allocations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of deductions, recharacterization of income, withholding-tax assessments, penalties for inadequate or missing documentation, and possible penalties based on transaction amounts or corrected taxable income. The French tax authority may apply the arm's-length principle and assess interest and aggravated penalties where intentional evasion is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil liability for tax losses caused by intentional misconduct or serious management errors and criminal liability where transfer-pricing manipulation forms part of fraudulent tax evasion. Individual exposure is heightened where directors approved false records or knowingly implemented sham arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, artificial substance, or treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SAS as a nominal invoicing vehicle without genuine French operations, appointing nominee directors, maintaining no effective control over matters, immediately distributing all receipts to a foreign affiliate, or claiming treaty benefits through a conduit lacking beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, withholding-tax reassessment, application of the principal-purpose test or abuse-of-law doctrine, corporate tax reassessment, interest, penalties, and possible permanent-establishment or transfer-pricing adjustments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability, criminal exposure for fraudulent declarations or money laundering where applicable, director disqualification, asset-freezing measures, and travel restrictions during investigations. Imprisonment may arise from associated fraud or laundering offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unauthorized practice of the legal profession
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SAS provides reserved legal advice, litigation representation, or advocacy in France without the required avocat status, bar registration, professional structure, professional insurance, or compliance with applicable French legal-profession rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal and professional sanctions may apply for unauthorized practice, including fines, injunctions, prohibition from continuing the activity, invalidity or unenforceability risks for certain arrangements, and referral to competent professional or judicial authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and individuals personally presenting themselves as French-qualified lawyers may face direct criminal liability, civil claims from clients, professional bans, damages, and potential imprisonment where the conduct constitutes a criminal offense. Limited liability does not shield the individual perpetrator.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Commingling client funds with operating funds, using a client account to finance the SAS, paying corporate expenses from client money, delaying remittance, or accepting client funds without the required regulated account and reconciliation controls.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restitution, civil damages, professional disciplinary action, account restrictions, regulatory reporting, and potential criminal prosecution for breach of trust, fraud, or money laundering. The exact sanction depends on whether the SAS is a regulated avocat structure and on the source and use of the funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, signatories, lawyers, and de facto managers may be personally liable for restitution and damages and may face criminal prosecution, professional disqualification, asset seizure, travel restrictions, and imprisonment for embezzlement, breach of trust, or laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify clients and beneficial owners, accepting unexplained third-party payments, ignoring sanctions or politically exposed person risks, failing to file a required suspicious-transaction report, or using litigation proceeds to disguise criminal assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory enforcement, fines, supervisory measures, account restrictions, professional discipline, confiscation, and criminal money-laundering or terrorist-financing sanctions. Suspicious transactions must be reported to TRACFIN where the entity is within the relevant regulated-profession perimeter.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may face personal criminal liability for knowing participation, facilitation, concealment, or serious compliance failures, together with asset confiscation, director bans, travel restrictions, and imprisonment under the applicable criminal provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Fictitious invoices, VAT fraud, and sham legal services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or receiving invoices for services not performed, reclaiming VAT on fictitious expenses, falsely describing cross-border legal services, or using circular invoices to move profits or funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, denial of input VAT, corporate tax adjustments, 40% or 80% penalties, late-payment interest, invoice-related fines, and criminal fraud or false-document sanctions where intentional conduct is proven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individuals who authorize or knowingly use false invoices may be personally prosecuted for tax fraud, forgery, fraud, or money laundering and may face restitution orders, asset seizure, travel restrictions, director disqualification, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Bribery, influence peddling, and judicial corruption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying or disguising payments to judges, public officials, arbitrators, court personnel, experts, counterparties, or intermediaries to obtain a litigation or enforcement advantage.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Severe criminal fines, confiscation, exclusion from public contracts, corporate compliance obligations, dissolution or prohibition measures in extreme cases, and imprisonment under French anti-corruption and criminal law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, employees, lawyers, and intermediaries may be personally prosecuted regardless of whether the payment was booked as a fee, success fee, commission, donation, or client expense. Personal fines, confiscation, disqualification, travel restrictions, and imprisonment may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to maintain statutory books and beneficial-owner information
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain accurate accounts, concealing the ultimate beneficial owner, filing false corporate information, omitting related-party transactions, or failing to preserve invoices, engagement letters, time records, and client-matter evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Accounting sanctions, tax reassessment, penalties for inaccurate corporate filings, beneficial-owner compliance enforcement, audit adjustments, and potential criminal consequences for false statements or concealment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president and de facto managers may face personal civil and criminal liability, including damages, disqualification from management, asset seizure, travel restrictions, and imprisonment where false statements, fraud, or laundering is established.
